subject: Geography
topic: Rivers of India — Origin, Course and Tributaries

questions.text: The Ganga river originates from which glacial source in Uttarakhand?

options.option_text: Yamunotri glacier — source of the Yamuna River
Gangotri glacier (Gomukh) — source of the Bhagirathi
Chorabari glacier — source of the Mandakini River
Milam glacier — source of the Goriganga tributary

questions.explanation: The Ganga originates at Gomukh ('cow's mouth'), the snout of the Gangotri glacier at ~3,900 m in Uttarakhand. The Bhagirathi River flows from Gangotri and is considered the principal headstream; it joins the Alaknanda at Devprayag to form the Ganga proper. The Yamunotri glacier is the source of the Yamuna, not the Ganga.

questions.text: The Brahmaputra River is known by which name as it flows through Tibet (China)?

options.option_text: Yarlung Tsangpo — its Tibetan name before the great bend
Jamuna — the name used for the river in Bangladesh downstream
Lohit — one of the Brahmaputra's Arunachal tributaries
Dibang — a major tributary that joins the Brahmaputra in Assam

questions.explanation: The Brahmaputra originates in Tibet as the Yarlung Tsangpo (also written Tsang Po). After making a dramatic hairpin turn (great bend) around Namcha Barwa peak, it enters Arunachal Pradesh as the Dihang, then becomes the Brahmaputra in Assam. In Bangladesh, it merges with the Ganga and is called the Jamuna.

questions.text: Most peninsular rivers flow eastward, but the Narmada flows westward into the Arabian Sea. What is the geological reason?

options.option_text: It originates in the Aravalli Range, which naturally slopes westward
It flows through a rift valley (graben) between the Vindhya and Satpura ranges
It was captured by the Indus drainage system during the Pleistocene
It follows the original westward drainage of Gondwana supercontinent

questions.explanation: The Narmada flows through a rift valley — an elongated depression formed by parallel faults — between the Vindhya Range (north) and Satpura Range (south). This structural graben channels it westward into the Gulf of Khambhat. The Tapi (Tapti) similarly flows west through its own rift valley. Other peninsular rivers draining east follow the tilt of the Deccan plateau.

questions.text: The Kaveri water dispute between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu exists primarily because ____.

options.option_text: Kaveri originates in Karnataka but its lower basin agriculture depends heavily on Tamil Nadu
Tamil Nadu built illegal upstream dams on the Kaveri without Karnataka's knowledge
The 1892 Cauvery Waters Agreement was declared void by the Supreme Court
Karnataka illegally diverts Kaveri water into the Krishna basin through canals

questions.explanation: The Kaveri originates in Karnataka (Coorg/Kodagu) but Tamil Nadu's delta agriculture — particularly the Thanjavur delta — has historically depended on its waters. Karnataka's development needs conflict with Tamil Nadu's historic water-use rights. The Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal (1990) and a Supreme Court ruling (2018) attempted to apportion flows but disputes continue, especially during drought years.

questions.text: Which of the following rivers does NOT drain into the Bay of Bengal?

options.option_text: Mahanadi — flows through Odisha into the Bay of Bengal
Godavari — flows through Andhra Pradesh to the Bay of Bengal
Tapti (Tapi) — flows westward into the Gulf of Khambhat
Krishna — flows through Andhra Pradesh to the Bay of Bengal

questions.explanation: The Tapti (Tapi) flows westward through its rift valley and drains into the Gulf of Khambhat (Arabian Sea) near Surat, Gujarat. Mahanadi (Odisha), Godavari (AP/Telangana), and Krishna (AP) are all east-flowing peninsular rivers draining into the Bay of Bengal. West-flowing peninsular rivers are rarer: Narmada, Tapti, Periyar, Sharavati.

questions.text: The Indus river originates in Tibet and enters India through Ladakh. Near Mithankot in Pakistan, it receives ____.

options.option_text: Only the Chenab alone, which is the single largest tributary meeting there
The combined Panjnad — waters of all five Punjab rivers (Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, Sutlej)
The Yamuna River, which was redirected westward following Siwalik Range tectonic uplift
The Beas alone, after the other four rivers join the Arabian Sea directly

questions.explanation: Near Mithankot (Pakistan), the Indus receives the Panjnad — the combined channel of the five Punjab rivers: Jhelum + Chenab (= Chenab), then Ravi, then Beas + Sutlej (= Sutlej), which all merge successively to form the Panjnad before joining the Indus. The Indus itself originates near Singi Khamban (Sengge Zangbo) in Tibet and enters India through Ladakh at Demchok.

questions.text: Which pairing of characteristics is CORRECTLY matched to the right river category?

options.option_text: Himalayan rivers: rain-fed only, non-perennial; Peninsular rivers: glacier-fed, perennial
Himalayan rivers: young, V-shaped gorges, high erosion; Peninsular rivers: old, graded, gentler gradient
Himalayan rivers: all flow west to the Arabian Sea; Peninsular rivers: all flow east to Bay of Bengal
Himalayan rivers: originate in Aravalli and Satpura; Peninsular rivers: originate in Himalayan glaciers

questions.explanation: Himalayan rivers are geologically young (post-Himalayan uplift, ~50 Ma), actively eroding, V-shaped valleys, and perennial (glacier + monsoon-fed). Peninsular rivers flow over ancient Gondwana rock, have graded profiles, wide flood plains, and are mostly rain-fed (seasonal). Option A reverses perenniality; Option C is wrong (Narmada, Tapti are westward peninsular rivers); Option D reverses the origins entirely.

questions.stem: Amarkantak, a sacred plateau in Madhya Pradesh, is celebrated as the source of the Narmada. Which other major river ALSO originates from the same Amarkantak hills?

options.option_text: Chambal, originating near Mhow in the Vindhya Range
Son, which flows northeast to merge with the Ganga
Betwa, a right-bank tributary of the Yamuna river
Wainganga, a tributary joining the Pranhita system

questions.explanation: B is correct: both the Narmada (westward) and the Son (eastward) spring from Amarkantak in the Maikal Hills of MP — a frequently tested PYQ fact. Chambal originates from the Vindhya Range near Janapav Hills/Mhow, and Betwa also rises from Vindhya near Bhopal; neither has any connection to Amarkantak.

questions.stem: The Beas river originates near the Rohtang Pass in Himachal Pradesh. Before the combined waters cross into Pakistan, the Beas merges with which river at the Harike wetland in Punjab?

options.option_text: Ravi, near the Shahpurkandi barrage in Punjab
Chenab, at the Trimmu confluence in the Punjab plains
Sutlej, forming the combined Beas-Sutlej link system
Jhelum, near the Pakistan-India border in Kashmir

questions.explanation: C is correct: the Beas joins the Sutlej at Harike in Punjab, India, and the combined flow then enters Pakistan. Harike is also a Ramsar-designated wetland. Ravi and Chenab join each other farther west inside Pakistan; Jhelum is a separate river in the western Indus system.

questions.stem: The Teesta river, at the centre of a long-pending water-sharing dispute between India and Bangladesh, drains through which pair of Indian states before joining the Brahmaputra in Assam?

options.option_text: Arunachal Pradesh and Meghalaya, draining the eastern hills
Sikkim and West Bengal, passing through Darjeeling district
Manipur and Nagaland, before entering the Brahmaputra valley
Uttarakhand and Bihar, draining the central Himalayan belt

questions.explanation: B is correct: the Teesta rises near Cho Lhamu lake in North Sikkim, cuts through Sikkim and then the Darjeeling–Jalpaiguri belt of West Bengal, and finally merges with the Brahmaputra in Assam. Arunachal Pradesh is a common distractor because it is associated with the Brahmaputra's own course, not the Teesta.

questions.stem: The Chambal river, infamous for the ravines (beehads) it carves across the Malwa plateau, eventually joins which river after forming part of the Madhya Pradesh–Rajasthan boundary?

options.option_text: The Ganga, at Allahabad (Prayagraj) in eastern UP
The Ken, forming a confluence near Banda in central UP
The Betwa, joining it near Hamirpur district in UP
The Yamuna, joining it near Etawah district in UP

questions.explanation: D is correct: after forming the MP–Rajasthan border, the Chambal enters UP and merges with the Yamuna near Etawah. Option A is the most tempting error — students confuse the Yamuna–Ganga chain and think Chambal meets Ganga directly; it does not. Ken and Betwa are also Yamuna tributaries but meet it farther upstream.

questions.stem: Which river of Rajasthan, popularly called 'Maru Ganga' (Ganga of the Desert), originates from the Aravalli hills near Ajmer and finally drains into the Rann of Kutch — NOT into any sea directly?

options.option_text: The Sabarmati, rising in the Aravalli and joining the Gulf of Khambhat
The Banas, a tributary of Chambal draining northeastern Rajasthan
The Luni, flowing southwest through the Thar Desert to Rann of Kutch
The Ghaggar, a seasonal river draining through Punjab and Haryana

questions.explanation: C is correct: the Luni ('salty river') is the lifeline of the Marwar desert, giving it the title Maru Ganga. It ends in the Great Rann of Kutch without reaching the sea. Sabarmati also originates in the Aravalli but drains into the Gulf of Khambhat and is never called Maru Ganga — this is the classic distractor that trips candidates.

questions.stem: The Mahi river of central-western India is cited in geography texts for a distinctive feature involving the Tropic of Cancer. Which statement accurately describes this phenomenon?

options.option_text: The Mahi originates south of the Tropic of Cancer and crosses it once into Gujarat
The Mahi takes a U-shaped turn and crosses the Tropic of Cancer at two distinct points
The Mahi's entire catchment lies north of the Tropic of Cancer across MP and Gujarat
The Tropic of Cancer passes exactly through the Mahi's source at the Vindhya plateau

questions.explanation: B is correct: the Mahi originates in the Malwa/Vindhya plateau of MP (approx 22.5°N), flows northward into Rajasthan crossing the Tropic of Cancer (23.5°N), then curves sharply westward and southwestward, crossing it a second time before draining into the Gulf of Khambhat. This double-crossing is a uniquely tested geographic fact. Option A is wrong because the river starts below the Tropic and crosses it twice, not once.

questions.stem: The Sharavathi river in Karnataka is celebrated for creating Jog Falls, India's highest plunge waterfall. Which description correctly identifies the Sharavathi's classification within India's river system?

options.option_text: A tributary of the Tungabhadra, draining eastward into the Bay of Bengal
A tributary of the Cauvery, joining it in Tamil Nadu before the Bay of Bengal
An independent west-flowing river draining into the Arabian Sea near Honnavar
A tributary of the Netravathi, draining into the Arabian Sea near Mangalore

questions.explanation: C is correct: the Sharavathi rises in the Western Ghats near Thirthahalli and flows westward as an independent river, creating the ~253 m Jog (Gersoppa) Falls before meeting the Arabian Sea at Honnavar in Uttara Kannada district. It is not a tributary of any major river. Option A (Tungabhadra) is the most tempting error because both rivers are in Karnataka, but Tungabhadra flows eastward into the Krishna system.
